E_cross_process_bs6.note: three separate python processes, fresh model load each time

verdict: MMLU scoring is EXACTLY reproducible within a fixed environment and batch size -- 3 in-process repeats and 3 separate processes all return 129/200. The only demonstrated sensitivity is BATCH COMPOSITION: batch sizes 4/6/8/16 give 131/129/131/129, a 2-item (1.0%) spread. TF32 is not implicated (129 both ways). n_rot 2 vs 4 differs (129 vs 127) but that is a different metric definition, not noise.
observed_divergence_attribution: The v8spc/small vs v6trace/ablate divergence (llama|occ_gender|s2) occurred at NOMINALLY IDENTICAL batch_size=6, so batch composition does not explain it. The remaining difference between those runs is the environment: the ablate panel was produced under transformers 5.14.1 and v8spc under 4.57.1 (the rebuild recorded in RESULTS_V8 2). This is consistent with the scoped determinism claim -- the edit CONSTRUCTION is bit-identical across that change, the MMLU EVALUATION is not. Not proven by re-running the old stack; stated as the residual explanation.
ws2_4_reproducibility_statement: Sweep-pipeline bit-determinism verified (108/108, results/x2 vs v6trace/x2, 0 differing). MMLU scoring is deterministic within a fixed environment and batch size (6/6 replicates identical) but exhibits batch-composition sensitivity of up to 1% (2 of 200 items); cross-version comparisons can differ by the same order. Fixed for v9 by scoring the gate in integer items, which removes the boundary knife-edge; NOT fixed at the source, which would require pinning batch composition and re-running.
